course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Project Practicum II: Software Engineering
course.description: This course introduces students to the practical application of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), focusing on how software is implemented, tested, deployed, and maintained in real-world environments. Students build core skills in Git-based version control, implementation practices (including code coverage and developer documentation), and a range of testing methodologies (functional and non-functional), concluding with deployment, maintenance and support (Business As Usual), and an introduction to the Secure Software Development Life Cycle (SSDLC). Throughout the semester, students apply what they learn directly to a team-based group project, producing real project artifacts such as branching workflows, test plans, deployment steps, and documentation.

clos.description: Apply version control and source code management practices using Git (branching, merging, tagging, environments, and software versioning) in a group project.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Demonstration + guided practice (Git workflow) Hands-on lab (branching/merging/conflict resolution) Pair programming / team-based repository workflow Project-based learning (apply Git in group project)
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Practical lab task: Git branching, merge, conflict resolution Repository audit (commit history, branching strategy, tags/releases) Mini-quiz (versioning, environments, SCM concepts) Peer evaluation on collaboration using Git

clos.description: Analyze implementation-phase challenges and implement solutions using code coverage, developer manual documentation, synchronous/asynchronous concepts, and appropriate framework vs. language choices.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Interactive lecture + case study (development phase challenges) Guided coding workshop (sync vs async, framework vs language decisions) Code review sessions (quality, maintainability) Tool-supported practice (code coverage tools, documentation standards)
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Implementation milestone (feature completion + clean code practices) Code coverage report + improvement evidence Developer Manual submission (setup/run/test instructions)

clos.description: Design and execute a comprehensive testing strategy by selecting testing methodologies, applying testing levels (unit/integration/system/user acceptance testing), and producing test reports covering functional and non-functional testing (performance/load/compatibility).
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Problem-based learning (testing problems from requirements/user stories) Workshop: test strategy design (methods + levels) Group activity: build test cases + test data- Peer review of test plan and test reports
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Test Plan + Test Cases (unit/integration/system/UAT) as project artifact Execution evidence (test results screenshots/logs) + defect report Test summary report (functional + non-functional: performance/load/compatibility) Group presentation/demo of testing outcomes

clos.description: Evaluate release readiness by planning deployment activities, defining maintenance and support (Business As Usual) tasks, and integrating Secure Software Development Life Cycle practices to reduce operational and security risks in the group project.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Seminar + discussion: deployment readiness & operational responsibility Role-based learning: DevOps/support roles (incident response, maintenance tasks) Checklist-driven workshop (release checklist, SSDLC checklist) Project coaching (release planning + risk management)
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Deployment plan + deployment demonstration (staging/production simulation) Maintenance & Support (Business As Usual) plan (monitoring/logging/backup/issue handling) SDLC checklist + risk mitigation summary Reflection report / team report on responsibilities and process organization

topics.title: Topic 1: Version Control System
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the purpose of Version Control Systems and Source Code Management in collaborative software development. LLO2: Apply Git commands to create repositories, commit changes, and manage branches using an agreed branching strategy. LLO3: Resolve merge conflicts and integrate changes from multiple team members using pull/merge workflows. LLO4: Implement software versioning and release tagging practices (e.g., tags/changelog) for the group project.

topics.title: Topic 2: Software Development Phase Or Implementation Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyze common challenges in the implementation phase and propose practical mitigation strategies (scope, quality, technical debt). LLO2: Differentiate frameworks and programming languages and justify an appropriate choice for the group project. LLO3: Apply synchronous and asynchronous concepts to implement features appropriately (based on performance and responsiveness needs). LLO4: Measure and improve code quality using code coverage results and produce a clear Developer Manual for project onboarding. LLO5: Review the group project progress against planned milestones and identify gaps in scope, quality, or timeline. LLO6: Evaluate the team’s Git workflow evidence (commits, branches, pull requests) and provide improvement feedback. LLO7: Assess implementation quality using code standards, coverage results, and documentation completeness (Developer Manual). LLO8: Formulate an action plan (task list + priorities) to address feedback and improve the next development iteration.

topics.title: Topic 3: Testing Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the role of testing within SDLC and identify key challenges in the testing phase. LLO2: Classify testing methodologies and select suitable approaches for a given software scenario. LLO3: Construct a test plan aligned to requirements/user stories including entry/exit criteria and defect handling. LLO4: Apply testing levels (unit, integration, system, UAT) to the group project and document results.

topics.title: Topic 4: Types of Testing
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Differentiate functional and non-functional testing and choose the correct type for different risks and requirements. LLO2: Design functional test cases and acceptance criteria for key features in the group project. LLO3: Execute performance/load/compatibility tests using appropriate tools/scripts and record evidence. LLO4: Evaluate testing outcomes and produce a test summary report including defects, severity, and recommendations.

topics.title: Topic 5: Deployment Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe deployment activities, environments (staging/production), and common deployment risks. LLO2: Prepare a deployment plan including configuration steps, rollback strategy, and release checklist. LLO3: Perform a basic deployment for the group project to a target environment (or simulation) and verify success. LLO4: Evaluate release readiness using deployment evidence and operational checks.

topics.title: Topic 6: Maintenance and Support Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain maintenance types (corrective/adaptive/perfective/preventive) and support responsibilities after release. LLO2: Develop a Business As Usual support plan (monitoring, logging, backup, ticket handling, incident steps). LLO3: Prioritize maintenance tasks based on severity, impact, and risk to users/business operations. LLO4: Document maintenance procedures and report incidents using a structured template (issue, root cause, resolution).

topics.title: Topic 7: Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain why security must be integrated across SDLC and identify common software security risks. LLO2: Apply secure coding practices (input validation, authentication/authorization awareness, secrets handling) in the group project. LLO3: Perform a basic security review using an SSDLC checklist and recommend mitigations. LLO4: Evaluate the project’s security readiness and justify risk-reduction decisions.

topics.title: Topic 8: Group project presentation and Feedback
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Organize project evidence in the Git repository (commits, branches, tags, releases) to demonstrate team workflow. LLO2: Present the project progress and workflow clearly using repository history and documented artifacts. LLO3: Respond to feedback by improving repository practices (naming conventions, branching discipline, documentation). LLO4: Reflect on team collaboration and summarize lessons learned for future development iterations.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
